answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to stake a refundable deposit that is slashed on proven fraud, with reputation earned only through verified work over time. A new inlet for participants demands the stake before any agent can transact, so creating thousands of fake identities means locking real capital in each one. Honest agents build a track record that peers can echo as endorsements, while a nebula of throwaway accounts with no history and no stake stays untrusted and cannot flood the market cheaply.
